nodes.label: Capacity Is a Rating Only at a Specified Radius
nodes.author: Chief Engineer (crane and rigging), Safety & Compliance
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.norm_label: capacity is a rating only at a specified radius
nodes.rationale: Load charts and the standards behind them (ASME B30.5, BS 7121, EN 13000) state capacity at a specified radius; linear interpolation between charted points is the industry's own reading of the table, but outside the charted span there is no rating at all.

nodes.label: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.author: Chief Engineer (crane and rigging), Safety & Compliance
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001 rated capacity comes only from a charted point

nodes.label: ADR-0002 A Plan States Two Checks: the Chart and the Booked Crane
nodes.author: Chief Engineer (crane and rigging), Safety & Compliance
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002 a plan states two checks: the chart and the booked crane

nodes.label: Out-of-Chart Radius Refusal
nodes.author: Chief Engineer (crane and rigging), Safety & Compliance
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.rationale: A lookup outside the chart's own span is refused and the refusal names the range the chart rates, because a clamped figure asserts a capacity nobody published and renders 'not rated' and 'within limit' identically - the highest-severity defect class in this product. Publishing the clamped number with an 'unrated' flag was rejected: a flag beside a number that gets typed into a permit is not a control. Only the chart in charge is read, so a mirrored manual row cannot refuse a radius the workbook answers.

nodes.label: Booked Rating Check Against gross / 0.75
nodes.author: Chief Engineer (crane and rigging), Safety & Compliance
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.rationale: The chart figure depends on the boom and radius in use, so a machine can pass the chart check while still being too small for the lift - the chart answers 'here', not 'at all'. The booked rating is therefore checked against the same required capacity (gross / 0.75), governs when it fails, and the chart figure stays visible so both the machine booked and the capacity at radius are seen. With no rating entered the plan says 'Not checked' rather than inventing a pass.

nodes.label: Community Impact Enforcement Ladder
nodes.rationale: Four graduated responses - correction, warning, temporary ban, permanent ban - each keyed to community impact, so moderation consequences are proportional and predictable.

nodes.label: Five Calculation Forms Over One Shared Lift
nodes.norm_label: five calculation forms over one shared lift

nodes.label: Rust Calculation Engine Ported from Android Kotlin
nodes.norm_label: rust calculation engine ported from android kotlin
nodes.rationale: The Rust engine is a line-for-line port of the Android Kotlin source and the tests carry the Kotlin suite's own expected literals, so any drift in the arithmetic fails the build.

nodes.label: 75% Rule Capacity Band
nodes.rationale: The chart check is deliberately a band, not a cap: at or under 75% of charted capacity the plan reads WITHIN LIMIT, 75-100% CAUTION, above 100% WARNING. When no booked rating is entered the plan says 'Not checked' rather than inventing a pass, so an absent rating can never be read as approval.

nodes.label: Threat Surface: xlsx Reading, Report Write, Embedded Web View
nodes.norm_label: threat surface: xlsx reading, report write, embedded web view
nodes.rationale: The app runs entirely on the user's machine, does not phone home and stores nothing between launches, so the surface is small: reading .xlsx load charts, writing the saved HTML report, and the embedded Tauri web view.

nodes.label: Council Review Requirement for Pull Requests
nodes.norm_label: council review requirement for pull requests

nodes.label: Standing Vetoes (Domain Safety and Application Security)
nodes.norm_label: standing vetoes (domain safety and application security)
nodes.rationale: The Domain Safety Engineer's veto on computed figures, limits, verdicts or wording presenting one, and the Application Security Engineer's veto on release integrity, stand even against a unanimous council; the chair breaks ties on process, not substance.

nodes.label: 8-of-10 Council Review Bar
nodes.rationale: A change proceeds only when every participating seat scores 8.0 or more and the mean is at least 8.0; 8 means 'no material defect and evidence on file', not 'looks fine'. Nothing is waived - if the fix is out of scope the scope is cut.

nodes.label: Solo-Maintainer Review Path
nodes.rationale: The council is one maintainer; that does not lower the bar, it changes who performs the passes. Each seat may run as a separate independent pass (different reader, fresh context, written rubric), the implementer never scores their own work, and if no independent pass exists the change does not land.

nodes.label: Domain Safety Engineer Seat
nodes.rationale: Owns anything that changes a computed figure, a capacity verdict, a limit, a warning or the way any of them is presented, including prose that describes them; blocks when a figure changes without a named source, a limit is softened, an example could be read as an approval, or the scope of use is missing.

nodes.label: window.uilog Tauri log bridge
nodes.rationale: Logging is wrapped in try/catch and degrades to a no-op when the Tauri bridge is absent, so a logging failure can never break the app.

nodes.label: Independent scroll panes on wide windows
nodes.norm_label: independent scroll panes on wide windows
nodes.rationale: Splitting a tab into a form column and a results column that scroll separately keeps one side in place while the other moves; stacked narrow windows keep the single scroll so small screens are not fragmented.

nodes.label: Rail footer pinned beneath the icon rail
nodes.norm_label: rail footer pinned beneath the icon rail
nodes.rationale: App name, version and contact stay visible at every window size; the navigation list scrolls on its own so product identity is never pushed off-screen.

nodes.label: Scope of use — calculation aid, not a certified lift plan
nodes.norm_label: scope of use — calculation aid, not a certified lift plan
nodes.rationale: Stated on every release so the tool is never mistaken for an approval: it aids a competent person and is not a certified lift plan.

nodes.label: One consistent 60/40 two-column layout on every tab
nodes.norm_label: one consistent 60/40 two-column layout on every tab
nodes.rationale: Every tab fills the same width instead of shrinking to fit its own content, so the app stops looking like a different product per tab; the Summary tab mirrors to 40/60 so the report preview gets the wider column.

nodes.label: Double scroll engages at the same breakpoint as the two-column cut
nodes.norm_label: double scroll engages at the same breakpoint as the two-column cut
nodes.rationale: The split cut trailed the two-column cut by 20 pixels, leaving a band where cards sat side by side with a single page scroll; matching the two cuts removes that dead zone.

nodes.label: AppImage zsync delta updates
nodes.rationale: A .AppImage.zsync sidecar lets appimageupdatetool fetch only changed blocks instead of the whole file; the first upgrade to 2.2.0 still has to be downloaded by hand.

nodes.label: Windows 10/11 build (WiX MSI and NSIS setup)
nodes.norm_label: windows 10/11 build (wix msi and nsis setup)

nodes.label: ResizeObserver loop error treated as benign warning
nodes.norm_label: resizeobserver loop error treated as benign warning
nodes.rationale: WebKitGTK reports the always-recoverable 'ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications' through the error event; the banner was alarming users for a harmless condition, so the redraw is deferred to the next animation frame and the message is logged rather than shown.

nodes.label: Jib configuration card (boom length / + jib / + extended jib)
nodes.norm_label: jib configuration card (boom length / + jib / + extended jib)

nodes.label: Reset to Crane Tab button (Graph tab)
nodes.norm_label: reset to crane tab button (graph tab)

nodes.label: 75% rule
nodes.rationale: The boom angle that satisfies the 75% rule at the farthest reach is chosen automatically, mirroring how the working radius is suggested for the main boom.

nodes.label: Workbook crane location on axis (X, Y) cell
nodes.norm_label: workbook crane location on axis (x, y) cell
nodes.rationale: Reading the crane's position, the longest main boom and the jib sheets means the newer workbook format is honoured instead of typed around; older workbooks without the cell fall back to the main-boom matrix on their own.

nodes.label: Update check is the only network call (no plan telemetry)
nodes.norm_label: update check is the only network call (no plan telemetry)
nodes.rationale: Nothing about the user or the plan is sent and no plan is stored between launches, so there is nothing to migrate and nothing sensitive to leak.

nodes.label: Download & install action on Windows
nodes.rationale: The installer must replace the running files, so the app fetches the installer, starts it and then closes itself; the AppImage is only reminded because appimageupdatetool already delta-updates it.

nodes.label: Booked crane rating check
nodes.rationale: The lift is checked against the crane the job actually booked, not only the point the load chart rates, so a crane too small for the lift can no longer pass because the chart reads high; an unrated crane reads 'Not checked'.

nodes.label: Chart tables list only the radii a boom column charts
nodes.norm_label: chart tables list only the radii a boom column charts
nodes.rationale: Repeating the last charted capacity down the remaining workbook radii, or publishing the previous boom's capacity under a new boom's label, invents figures the chart never rated.

nodes.label: Example load charts in docs/examples/ (TR-350M-1, TL-200M)
nodes.norm_label: example load charts in docs/examples/ (tr-350m-1, tl-200m)

nodes.label: Plan details card (reference, prepared/checked/approved by)
nodes.rationale: A checked calculation is expected to carry its authorship and issue date, so the fields print at the top of the plan with blank lines included, letting a printed copy be signed.

nodes.label: Working radius outside the load chart is refused
nodes.norm_label: working radius outside the load chart is refused
nodes.rationale: The old lookup clamped the nearest charted capacity in from either end; the carried figure was never a rating the chart published, so a radius (or jib boom angle) outside the charted range is now refused and the plan states the refusal in its crane section.

nodes.label: Workbook unit declaration parsing ('Unit: ton')
nodes.rationale: Small charts written in kg were previously read as tonnes, understating usage a thousand times; the declared unit text now wins and the magnitude guess is kept only for charts that declare nothing.

nodes.label: Capacity verdict band (WITHIN LIMIT / CAUTION / WARNING)
nodes.norm_label: capacity verdict band (within limit / caution / warning)
nodes.rationale: The verdict gets its own coloured band directly under the figures it judges and before the working that produced them, so the answer on the printed first page is read before the arithmetic.

nodes.label: A4 print margin guidance (leave dialog on Default)
nodes.norm_label: a4 print margin guidance (leave dialog on default)
nodes.rationale: The page sets its own one-inch A4 margin, but the dialog's Minimum and None options override any document margin, so Default is the only setting that preserves the layout.

nodes.label: TL-200M specification sheet (8.0 m jib)
nodes.rationale: A copied example is reference data, so a figure in it matters more than any layout change; the workbook now charts the jib the manufacturer specifies (8.0 m, not 7.2 m) and the specification PDF ships beside it so every figure can be checked against the source.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: Fonts may be bundled, embedded and sold with software but not sold by themselves, derivatives may not use the Reserved Font Name, and the requirement to stay under the OFL does not extend to documents created with the fonts.

nodes.label: Startup error banner fallback
nodes.rationale: Any failure before or during boot is painted on the page instead of leaving a blank window, so a broken module or missing asset always produces a readable sentence rather than a silent empty app.

nodes.label: Release Cut Process
nodes.rationale: A release is created as a draft with all assets attached and only then made public, so a partial upload never reaches a user; the draft is deleted before a rerun because published bytes are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Draft-First Publish with Immutable Assets
nodes.rationale: Publish creates a draft, asserts the four named assets, uploads with overwrite_files: false, then flips the draft public; a failure leaves a hidden draft, so a partial upload never reaches a user and the rerun path stays idempotent.

nodes.label: One Release-Notes File per Tag
nodes.rationale: The v2.5.1 page repeated 2.5.0 and 2.4.0 because RELEASE_NOTES.md held the last three versions and the publish job used the whole file as the body. One notes file per tag, published as exactly that file, makes a repeated body structurally impossible instead of a matter of author discipline.

nodes.label: Release Gate Comparing Tag, Version, Notes and Record
nodes.norm_label: release gate comparing tag, version, notes and record

nodes.label: publish-release-notes.sh One-Time Repair Script
nodes.rationale: Republishes the 13 already-published pages from docs/releases/; dry-run by default and --yes to write, so it is safe to repeat. Retire it once the 13 pages are republished, or it becomes a permanent script for a finished job.

nodes.label: Deliberate Release Page Absences
nodes.rationale: No screenshots (the readme carries them), no in-app changelog (the update reminder opens the GitHub release page), no signing (SHA256SUMS.txt travels the same connection, so it catches corruption, not compromise). Stating the absences stops a reader assuming a guarantee that does not exist.
nodes.source_location: What a release page deliberately does not do

nodes.label: Council Record 0001: One Release-Notes File per Tag
nodes.norm_label: council record 0001: one release-notes file per tag

nodes.label: Portable Ubuntu 22.04 AppImage Build (glibc 2.35 Floor)
nodes.rationale: A host build links the host's glibc and bundles its GTK/WebKitGTK, so an AppImage built on a rolling-release system refuses to start on an older LTS ('GLIBC_2.44 not found'). The portable build runs inside an Ubuntu 22.04 userspace (bubblewrap) to fix the floor at glibc 2.35, the widest compatibility.

nodes.label: v2.5.0 Entry: Booked Rating Check and Rated Envelope
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.norm_label: v2.5.0 entry: booked rating check and rated envelope

nodes.label: Two Stores: ADR for Product Decisions, Record for Reviews
nodes.community_name: ADR-0001 Rated Capacity Comes Only from a Charted Point
nodes.norm_label: two stores: adr for product decisions, record for reviews
nodes.rationale: docs/adr/ answers 'why does the calculator behave this way' and is read when someone asks why the product does this; decisions/ answers 'why was this allowed to ship' - who sat, what they scored, what blocked. A council record links the ADRs it relies on; an ADR need not mention the council.

nodes.label: Release Notes File Shape
nodes.rationale: Fixed order - title, line of facts with the headline, highlights, Added/Changed/Fixed, compatibility, download table, scope line, footer - and words kept from CHANGELOG.md so the two never disagree. A reference-data correction leads because it outranks a layout change.

nodes.label: v2.5.1 Entry: Report Head Layout and TL-200M Chart Fix
nodes.norm_label: v2.5.1 entry: report head layout and tl-200m chart fix

nodes.label: Scope of Use (Calculation Aid, Not Certification)
nodes.norm_label: scope of use (calculation aid, not certification)
nodes.rationale: The product is a calculation aid for a competent person planning a lift; it does not certify the lift, crane, operator or plan, and is not a substitute for the manufacturer's load chart, the site's lift plan procedure, or rigger judgement. Stated so a printed plan is never mistaken for an approved lift plan.
